name: Pleomorphic Liposarcoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Soft Tissue Tumors

criteria.description: Presence of pleomorphic lipoblasts with marked nuclear atypia and multinucleation on histological examination
Immunohistochemical staining positive for S100 protein in lipoblasts and negative for MDM2 amplification
Imaging showing large, heterogeneous soft tissue mass with areas of necrosis and fat density

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of pleomorphic lipoblasts with nuclear atypia plus supportive immunohistochemical profile
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing to exclude other liposarcoma subtypes is recommended

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapidly enlarging deep soft tissue mass with irregular margins
searchTerms: fast-growing deep tissue lump with uneven edges
quickly enlarging soft tissue tumor with irregular borders
rapidly expanding deep mass with jagged margins

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of palpable firm nodules within the tumor mass

common.symptomName: Localized swelling and mass effect symptoms
searchTerms: swelling in one area causing pressure symptoms

common.symptomName: Pain or tenderness at tumor site
Restricted range of motion if tumor involves extremities
searchTerms: limited joint movement due to tumor
reduced range of motion near tumor
open skin wound on tumor site

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to nerve compression

rare.symptomName: Distant metastases presenting with respiratory symptoms

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be elevated
imaging: MRI showing heterogeneous soft tissue mass with fat signal intensity and necrotic areas
CT scan demonstrating large soft tissue mass with irregular borders and possible calcifications
genetic: Absence of MDM2 and CDK4 amplification differentiates from well-differentiated/dedifferentiated liposarcoma
Complex karyotype with multiple chromosomal abnormalities
other: Histopathology revealing pleomorphic lipoblasts with marked nuclear atypia
Immunohistochemistry positive for S100 protein in tumor cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of MDM2 and CDK4 amplification
Less pleomorphic cells and more uniform spindle cell areas
Myxoid stroma with uniform round to oval cells

redFlags: Rapid tumor growth over weeks to months
Neurological deficits due to nerve compression
Unexplained weight loss and systemic symptoms
references: WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone, 5th Edition, 2020
Fletcher CDM, Bridge JA, Hogendoorn PCW, Mertens F. WHO Classification of Tumours of Soft Tissue and Bone. IARC; 2013.
